cells.tense: A direction is being chosen now and the grip on the old one is already open.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: When something pushes you to turn back, say to whoever is pushing what you chose, once. Then stay where you said.
cells.core:
What you're pointed at is chosen, and it holds because you keep choosing it rather than defending it. The heading came from genuine engagement — the feeling moved first and the direction followed — so you don't have to re-decide it every morning. That's what a direction looks like going well, and it's bending toward the push that will come.

What comes with this is momentum you can spend, and the place to spend it is where the pressure lands. When someone or something leans on you to turn back, don't argue the whole case. Say what you chose, once, and stay on it. The saying is the whole defence that day. You'll find out quickly whether the heading is really yours, and you'll have kept it while finding out.

cells.tense: Tomorrow's version of this is already decided and the hands have not caught up.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Give an afternoon to one thing these months grew, the way it stands now rather than what you'll do with it.
cells.core:
The connection is being written ahead of itself. You can see where it lands, how it goes, what it turns into, and the rehearsing runs far enough in front that the actual day arrives as a small surprise. Part of this is being managed toward an outcome that hasn't happened. What's underneath is real — something is here — and the readiness is outrunning the thing it's ready for.

What's scarce is time spent on what already grew. Take one thing these months produced, the connection or the work or the change, and give an afternoon to it exactly as it stands. Not what you'll do with it. What's here, enjoyed and used and sat in. For one afternoon the coming stretch doesn't need managing, and you'll come back knowing what's actually in your hands.

cells.tense: A door closed behind you and you are still standing at it.
cells.act: hold many truths at once without collapsing them
cells.ask: Put the pulls on you down on paper, four or five, with whose each one is beside it. Settle none of them this week.
cells.core:
A connection ended or changed, and you haven't moved off the spot. Something finished and the finishing didn't get taken in, so the pull keeps going toward a door that isn't there anymore. What's drained is the sense of what's actually so — the same reach happening without landing on anything.

So decide nothing yet. Set the pulls on you down on paper, four or five of them, and mark which are yours and which you picked up somewhere else. Hold all of them at once without sorting them into one answer. Several can be true together, and seeing that is what lets the step go. Nothing has to be released this week; it only has to be seen, exactly as many things as it is.

cells.tense: Something is being set down here and the hand doing it calls itself nothing.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: When someone describes being stuck where you stood, tell them once what the way out looked like for you — then stop talking.
cells.core:
Something gets set down around you, and the setting down doesn't get claimed. When people ask how you got through what you got through, the answer is a shrug and a maybe-it-just-happened. The moving-on is real, and it does something for the people watching it. What's missing is only the acknowledgment that a hand was on it, and that hand was yours.

The whole act is one sentence. When someone describes being stuck where you stood, say what the way out looked like, plainly, once, then stop — no following them in, no checking whether they took it. Pointing at a passage you can see doesn't make you responsible for anyone's walk through it. The line between showing and steering is the one worth knowing, and you learn it by stopping after the pointing.
